newsitem.title: CANADA: Potash Corp shares up on price rise plans.
newsitem.headline: Potash Corp shares up on price rise plans.

text.p: Shares in Potash Corp of Saskatchewan surged in Toronto and New York on Tuesday after the company told clients it planned to raise domestic potash prices in mid-February, an analyst said.

"Basically they're going into a fill program right now and will raise prices in the middle of February. So it gives people an incentive to buy right now," J.P. Morgan Securities analyst Donald Carson said.
"With inventory levels being lower than year-ago levels, there is an expectation that some or all of this price increase may hold," he added.

Potash has not yet made a formal announcement or issued a new price list, but Carson said the domestic price would be increased to US$84 a ton for coarse grade, free on board (FOB), potash from US$76 on February 17.
FOB describes how the potash is sold to the customer. "There are two ways to sell (potash). You can sell it FOB at the mine or you can deliver it to the customer," Carson said.
Potash shares rose 4.05 to 107.50 on the Toronto Stock Exchange and climbed 3-1/8 to 79-5/8 on the New York Stock Exchange in mid-afternoon.
